title: Why Honey Never Spoils
short_title: Why Honey Never Spoils (It Can Last Thousands of Years)
description: Honey can sit in a cupboard for thousands of years and still be safe to eat. Here is the simple science: sugar that sucks water out of germs, acid, and a natural germ killer made by bees. Never give honey to babies under 1 year old.
comment: Which food do you think should last forever? Tell me below!

scenes.text: Honey can sit in a cupboard for thousands of years and still be safe to eat. How is that even possible?
First, honey is about eighty percent sugar and less than twenty percent water. And germs need water to live.
When a germ lands in honey, the sugar pulls the water right out of its body. It shrivels up like a raisin. This is called osmosis.
Second, honey is acidic, which germs do not like.
Third, bees add an enzyme that slowly makes a tiny bit of hydrogen peroxide, a natural germ killer.
One catch: keep the lid tight, because wet honey can spoil. And never give honey to babies under one year old.
